tasks.title: The reserve total is the sum of its per-bill amounts, so the derived divisor needs an owner decision
tasks.detail: DISCOVERED 2026-09-19 by the OS-054 live verification, and it contradicts D-013's stated premise. D-013 permits an even split of 'total set aside funds' across the reserve's bills on the owner's belief that 'Bill reserve is a single bucket, I'm not sure how it allocates per bill in Crew currently'. The live data shows Crew does allocate per bill: of the five bills in reserve BillReserve:8d2f3e8f-..., Rent reports reservedAmount 1097.10 and the other four report 0.00 each -- explicitly reported, not absent, since reserved_amount_reported = 1 on all five -- and totalReservedAmount = 1097.10 is exactly their SUM. Two consequences. (a) The derived fallback is dormant on this data: precedence stops at observed, so the owner-approved 'Meridian estimate, split across N bills' copy currently appears nowhere, and it will only ever appear when a bill in a reserve has no reported amount while the reserve total is known. (b) If it did fire, dividing a total that is a sum would give an unreported bill a share of OTHER bills' money -- e.g. 1097.10 / 5 = 219.42 to a bill whose siblings already account for the whole bucket. Candidate rules for the owner to choose from: (i) only divide when NO bill in the reserve reports an amount (the total is then unallocated in Crew's own terms); (ii) subtract reported amounts from the total and divide only the remainder; (iii) drop the derived fallback entirely and show unknown for an unreported bill. Option (i) is the smallest change that removes the fabrication risk while keeping the copy the owner ratified. tasks.title: Fix the flaky credential-tampering test that carried an unexplained 1-in-256 failure
tasks.detail: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-09-20 while running the non-browser suite for an unrelated docs-only slice, which is how it surfaced: `tests/crew/test_session_credentials.py::test_cipher_rejects_tampering_and_wrong_key` failed once, then passed 5/5 in isolation, which is the signature of a nondeterministic defect rather than a real regression. ROOT CAUSE, proven by reproduction rather than reasoned about: the test built its tampered value as `encrypted.ciphertext[:-1] + b"x"`, which OVERWRITES the final byte instead of changing it. Whenever the ciphertext already ended in 0x78 -- the byte for 'x' -- the 'tampered' value was BYTE-IDENTICAL to the original, decryption correctly succeeded, and `pytest.raises(CredentialDecryptionError)` failed. A short reproduction found such a ciphertext on attempt 14 and printed 'old tamper is byte-identical to the original: True' and 'decrypt(tampered) -> NO ERROR', so the mechanism is demonstrated, not inferred. Frequency: the last byte must be 0x78, so roughly one run in 256 -- rare enough to look like noise, and it is a SECURITY test, where a spurious failure teaches people to ignore failures. FIX: flip the final byte with XOR (`bytes([encrypted.ciphertext[-1] ^ 0x01])`) so the tamper always changes something, plus an explicit `assert tampered_bytes != encrypted.ciphertext` guard so the test can never silently become a no-op again. VERIFIED: the same flip logic ran over 5000 fresh encryptions with ZERO failures to detect, the test passes 8/8 consecutive runs, the file is Ruff-clean, and the full non-browser suite is green at 1417 passed / 1 skipped. NOTE FOR TRIAGE HABITS: this is why 'a test failed but it passes on re-run' should be diagnosed rather than re-run until green -- the re-run was hiding a 0.4% false-alarm rate in a security assertion.

tasks.detail:
THE OWNER'S ORIGINAL MOTIVATION FOR MERIDIAN'S AI FEATURES, stated 2026-09-20 in his own words: 'the ability to say something like, I had to pay 500 dollars to repair my car, I cant cover this bill, look at the foreseeable future and make any budget/bill/autopilot adjustments necessary (proposals are then generated). I may add a stipulation like, I need at least 600 dollars free to spend each pay period, so meridian would make sure my pocket rule is for 600 dollars to free to spend.' THIS RECORDS THE TARGET; IT DOES NOT AUTHORISE BUILDING IT NOW. STATUS: open, deliberately unstarted, because its prerequisites are real and unmet. THE CAPABILITY, in three parts. (1) INPUT: an unforeseen cost plus a goal -- 'I paid 500 for the car', 'I cannot cover this bill'. (2) OWNER STIPULATIONS: standing constraints the plan must satisfy, e.g. a minimum free-to-spend per pay period, which would set the pocket rule to that amount. These are OWNER-SET POLICY held in Meridian (Crew has no equivalent field) and they BOUND THE PROPOSAL SPACE -- they are not a classifier output, they cannot remove an approval, and per the OS-056 rule nothing may ever turn a score into a path around owner approval. A stipulation that cannot be satisfied must produce a refusal or a plan that names what it cannot meet, never a silently weakened constraint. (3) OUTPUT: PROPOSALS across budget, bill and autopilot settings -- the 'one validated plan for the executor' already specified in roadmap I.3, never a debate transcript, never applied automatically. Every change carries its evidence, what it assumes, and what would change the answer; each is approved, executed and verified against the provider by readback. PREREQUISITES, in order, all recorded elsewhere: roadmap I.1 (envelope AND permissions; no role ever gets a provider write tool), I.2 (one role proven end to end, read-only and evidence-bound), I.3 (council producing one validated plan); Track C V2 (plan a paycheck without counting the same cash twice) and V3 (finish an authorised intervention and get an honest receipt); OS-059 (the connector readback gaps -- the sweep threshold and the pocket-allocation setting -- without which the pocket rule cannot be read, let alone reasoned about); and the existing propose -> approve -> execute -> readback engine, which is NOT to be rebuilt. WHAT IT MUST NOT DO: (1) never mutate anything -- it emits proposals; (2) never invent an owner stipulation, and never reinterpret one to a different number; (3) never present a plan as fact, a forecast as a balance, or a simulation as real money (D-013/D-015); (4) never assume the bill set or a due date is stable, since dates can move without the owner (Rent went 5th to 16th to 18th, the last not by him) and the bill set may change shape and revert; (5) never flag a payment-arrangement bill or a one-time bill as an error -- they are the owner's workarounds; (6) never model real-world lateness; (7) fail closed when the foreseeable future is underdetermined rather than filling the gap with a plausible number. FIRST ARTIFACT WHEN IT IS REACHED (framing corrected after the owner's design constraint): the OWNER STIPULATION store is a PRECONDITION, not the capability. It must exist as machine-readable owner policy so that a planner has a constraint to satisfy, and the read-only satisfaction checker is a useful deterministic TOOL. But per the owner's rule recorded in roadmap Track I -- 'An intelligence is needed because it shouldnt be prescribed to a preordained set of variables, virgil decides what needs to be done based on my input and proposes action' -- the DECISION of what needs doing is formed by an INTELLIGENCE reasoning over the actual situation, NEVER by a preordained variable set, a hardcoded decision table, or a lookup that maps a detected condition to a canned response. A design that can only act on anticipated cases has FAILED this task even if every test passes. Deterministic parts are TOOLS and CHECKS (arithmetic, stipulation satisfaction, freshness, provenance, readback verification): they make the output auditable and must never stand in for the decision itself. The review test is: could it handle a situation nobody wrote down? THE UNIFYING FRAME (owner, 2026-09-20): 'Thats the whole point of shortfall, virgils brief, proposals, automation. Its why almost full feature parity was so important. This was the whole point and vision all along.' So shortfall detection, Virgil's brief, the proposal engine and automation are ONE arc, not four features: detect a shortfall honestly -> analyse the foreseeable future -> generate proposals across every adjustable setting while honouring stipulations -> owner approves -> execute -> verify against the provider -> automate only what was explicitly preapproved. TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT CHANGE ORDERING: (a) FEATURE PARITY IS A PREREQUISITE, NOT POLISH -- Meridian must be able to READ AND ADJUST everything the owner can adjust in Crew (bills, reserves, pockets, autopilot rules, funding settings), because an adjustment it cannot read is one it cannot propose; this is why OS-059 sits ON this critical path rather than beside it. (b) VIRGIL IS THE FRONT DOOR to this arc, not a separate project: 'I should be able to ask virgil to analyze my financial situation and generate proposals to make all the in app adjustments I need to see me through, with any stipulations included' -- so VIRGIL-A1/A3 are the interface to OS-063, and A3's negative test (speech or model output can never select direct mutation provenance) is the safety property the whole arc rests on. NOTE ON INCOME TIMING, learned the hard way the same day: a paycheck's arrival day is a SEPARATE fact from a bill due date (the owner switched direct deposit to Crew, which has no early direct deposit, so income lands later while Rent stayed on the 16th) -- funding-event timing follows income arrival, never the due date, and Meridian must state what it OBSERVED rather than assert who caused a change. THE PROACTIVE HALF (owner, 2026-09-20), which is Track C V4 carrying this task's payload: 'I noticed you had to spend an extra 500 on ____, I propose to do these things to stay solvent without being cash starved in the meantime, and then return to steady state on this date, with your approval, I'll take care of all of it.' Four requirements the reactive form does not have: (1) MERIDIAN NOTICES -- the trigger is an OBSERVED deviation, not a request; (2) SOLVENCY AND LIQUIDITY ARE BOTH GOALS -- 'without being cash starved in the meantime' makes the liquidity floor INTEGRAL, so a plan that rebuilds the reserve by starving spendable cash is not a solution but the failure it was meant to prevent; (3) THE PLAN NAMES A RECOVERY DATE -- a plan with no end date is not a plan; (4) APPROVAL THEN EXECUTION -- one approval authorises the whole plan, Meridian executes it and the receipt is honest, with no part of the plan exempt from the gate. PREREQUISITES ADDED: V4's suppression/dedupe/feedback lifecycle is a PREREQUISITE, not a detail, because proactivity is where alert storms become the live risk -- note meridian/proactive.py is already wired but its lifecycle is UNVERIFIED in docs/project/CONCEPT_COVERAGE.md; the detection side must obey the OS-056 rule (a classifier may only ADD friction); and the natural front door for the proactive offer is VIRGIL-A4, gated by the addendum on C-V4 plus one proven I.2 role.

Owner's words: 'the stipulation floor is going to be a moving target until I catch up and get to a steady state budget.' So it is a TIME-VARYING owner-set policy value, NOT an unknown-but-fixed number waiting to be decided, and NOT $600. CONSEQUENCES: (1) the stipulation store must be APPEND-WITH-VALIDITY, not one mutable scalar -- each floor carries the window over which it applies and a superseded floor is RETAINED, so the system can state what the floor WAS at any past time (the project's own 'absence is recorded, not deleted' discipline). (2) The satisfaction checker must state the position against the floor IN FORCE AT THE TIME BEING EVALUATED, never against 'the' floor, or a plan will be judged by a rule the owner had not set yet. (3) NEVER extrapolate the trend or invent a steady-state target the owner has not stated: the floor rises because the owner is steering it, there is no forward curve to fit, and an inferred destination is absence-as-assertion. (4) DIRECT TENSION WITH THIS TASK'S OWN PROACTIVE REQUIREMENT: the proactive form must name a recovery date, but recovery is defined relative to a destination and the destination is moving, so that requirement must FAIL CLOSED -- say the recovery position is not determinable while the floor is still moving rather than name a date built on an invented target. Do NOT hardcode a floor into code, a test, a fixture or a doc, and do not pin the current value as a rule (D-015 'owner adjustments are data, not law' applied to a stipulation). The CADENCE half IS settled and needs no owner input: income is 'Veterans Home', 1663.00, cadence biweekly (crew_funding_plans, read 2026-09-20), so 'pay period' means biweekly. Full accounting in docs/project/EVIDENCE_PIPELINE_TRIAGE_2026-09-20.md; read it before acting. (1) GMAIL IS NOT BEING PULLED, BECAUSE NOTHING PULLS IT: POST /api/meridian/gmail/intake (meridian/api.py:685) is a MANUAL backfill and NO frontend code calls it (grep for gmail/intake in static/js and templates returns nothing); the only automatic refresh is Crew (meridian/refresh.py, and the live log shows provider=crew status=complete repeatedly). Credentials are NOT the blocker: connection_authorizations shows gmail|connected and calendar|connected, and oauth_tokens holds 5 Gmail + 1 calendar rows, ALL WITH A REFRESH TOKEN. (2) CALENDAR IS WORSE THAN 'NOT PULLED' -- IT IS WIRED TO NOTHING: meridian/connectors/calendar.py is a real read-only connector, but the only references to it anywhere are imports of READ_ONLY_CALENDAR_SCOPE for OAuth (meridian/api.py:1054, app.py:129). There is no calendar intake route and no caller of its ingestion, yet a calendar OAuth token exists with a refresh token, created 2026-09-06 -- so consent was granted and never used. (3) THE VIEWER FAILURE HAS A PRECISE ROOT CAUSE: THE BLOB STORE IS EMPTY. The live log shows a real 404 -- 'GET /api/meridian/evidence/616/content HTTP/1.1" 404' (19/Sep/2026 03:53:48) -- and meridian/api.py:1370 returns evidence_content_missing ('This document's content is not stored yet. It was created before content was persisted; re-run the mail intake to backfill it.'). Measured: 732 rows, ALL 732 carrying a non-empty content_hash, ALL 732 with size_bytes>0, and ZERO files in the evidence blob store; no row has content_deleted_at or revoked_at set, so nothing was deleted or swept -- the content was NEVER WRITTEN. This is an ALREADY-PARTIALLY-FIXED past defect: meridian/ingest.py:79-86 now treats a duplicate as a repair opportunity and persists the blob anyway ('a prior run may have created the metadata row before blob storage was wired'), both routes now pass a blob store (api.py:707 and :678), and EncryptedBlobStore.put is content-addressed by sha256 so a re-run is IDEMPOTENT. The blob store itself was VERIFIED FUNCTIONAL by an encrypted put/read round-trip on a scratch root. THREE RISKS IN THE OBVIOUS FIX, and the first must be handled BEFORE re-running: (a) A 14-DAY WINDOW OF MAIL MAY BE PERMANENTLY UNRECOVERABLE -- since_days=30 and max_messages_per_account=50 are HARDCODED and not request parameters, the original window was 2026-08-07 to 2026-09-06 while a re-run today covers 2026-08-21 to 2026-09-20, so mail dated 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-20 is outside the new window and would stay unreadable even after a successful backfill. (b) THE FAILURE IS SILENT -- the duplicate-path blob write is wrapped in 'except Exception: pass' (ingest.py:85-86), so a failed write still reports state=ingested/duplicate=true and tells the owner it worked; the ONLY trustworthy check is the blob COUNT ON DISK, never the route's response. (c) THE KEY IS DERIVED FROM app.secret_key (app.py:116-120), so if that changed, earlier blobs are undecryptable and read() raising is reported as the same 'not stored yet' 404 -- indistinguishable to the owner from the current condition. (4) SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND WHILE TRIAGING -- BILLS ARE NOT LINKED TO EVIDENCE: evidence_links holds 15 links total and ALL 15 target transaction/documents; ZERO target a bill despite 11 bills in the DB, and only 8 distinct evidence items of 732 are linked to anything. Gmail intake populates link_mail_evidence_to_transactions (meridian/gmail_intake.py:157) and there is NO bill equivalent, so fixing the blob store alone will NOT make bill evidence appear. RECOMMENDED ORDER: widen the intake window FIRST, then re-run Gmail intake, then verify by counting blobs on disk; then make the silent blob-write failure visible; then treat calendar as a new-capability decision (which events become evidence, and under what linking rule) rather than a patch; then the bill-to-evidence linking gap. The roadmap named OS-067 only in the 2026-09-21 in-flight note, without a track, which is the gap this assignment closes.)

slices.item: OS-067 calendar leg — read-only calendar context, ingested through Composio as the sole adapter
slices.owner_decision: Owner, 2026-09-21, in three corrections that each changed the design: (1) scope -- calendar events are READ-ONLY CONTEXT, 'never matched to money'; (2) mechanism -- 'I want the calendar polled, once a day, and to be the only adaptor, but through composio'; (3) separation -- 'Two different mechanisms for email and calendar.' So the in-app Google OAuth transport is deliberately NOT built for calendar, and Meridian holds no Google credential for it and is not exposed to Google's refresh-token lifetime. Mail is untouched: its in-app connectors, filters and OAuth stay exactly as they were. The owner also defined the status semantics to show in Settings: 'For Composio (Live) will strictly mean the composio connection is still current with the harness, not that it is live and continuously polling.' This DECISION OPENED the roadmap section 12 entry 'Harness ingestion service' for calendar read-only context; section 12 is updated in the same commit, per its own rule 3.
slices.why_the_harness_path_is_right_here: The in-app path was blocked on a credential, not on code: all 5 Google refresh tokens fail with HTTP 400 because the OAuth app sits in 'Testing' publishing status, where Google expires refresh tokens after 7 days. Publishing to production fixes that, but the harness path removes the dependency entirely -- the Composio connection holds its own auth and is verified ACTIVE. D-016 already sanctions this surface and names this exact case as its canonical example.
slices.built: meridian/migrations/026_calendar_context.sql adds calendar_context_events; meridian/calendar_context.py is the canonical intake and its store; scripts/calendar_context_ingest.py is the feed entry point with the Composio-shaped transport. Both routes -- and there is now only one -- satisfy the SAME CalendarTransport interface the app already declared in meridian/connectors/calendar.py, and hand events to the SAME ingest function, so dedupe, provenance and the minimum-field rule cannot be bypassed by arriving from outside. This mirrors scripts/backfill_charge_evidence.py, the worked example D-016 guardrail 3 cites, and it is what keeps the route from being a side-channel write.
slices.the_boundary_is_enforced_by_absence: The scope decision is held in three places rather than by convention, and each has a test. (1) The table has NO amount, commitment, charge or transaction column, so matching cannot begin without a deliberate migration -- asserted by reading PRAGMA table_info and rejecting any such column name. (2) The module exposes no match/link/exposure/obligation/propose function -- asserted by walking its public surface. tasks.notes: Four design decisions. (1) The Skeptic carries the SAME SUBJECT KEY as the claim it addresses: without it the two claims cannot be compared and the conflict becomes invisible. tasks.title: Payday is settable in Settings and stays bidirectional with Crew
tasks.owner_raised: 2026-09-21, immediately after the payday row was added to the hub: 'payday needs to be in settings, we have all the machinery to have it mutatable through crew and through meridian, bidirectional, if it wasnt already. There is no other place to set this'.
tasks.detail: The hub row now reaches `?section=payday` (be98fc4), which settles REACHABILITY and not SETTABILITY. The owner's point is that Settings is the ONLY place this can be set, so the surface has to actually set it, and that a value changed in Crew must show in Meridian and a value changed in Meridian must reach Crew. What exists today is far short of that: meridian/api.py:1196 exposes `GET /settings/payday` and meridian/api.py:1216 exposes `POST /settings/payday/learning-floor` -- ONE writable field. Everything else the payday surface displays (cadence, the funding schedule, which funding event covers each bill) is derived from the Crew account rather than written back. So the machinery is partly there and must be inventoried before anything is claimed: 'if it wasnt already' is the whole question, and it is not yet answered.
tasks.progress: NOT STARTED, and the FIRST step is read-only inventory rather than a mutation: enumerate every payday field the surface displays, mark each one as derived-from-Crew, written-by-Meridian, or not-settable-at-all, and confirm against Crew which of those it can actually accept. Only then decide the write path. This must not begin by adding a control and discovering afterwards whether it can be honoured.
acceptance_criteria: Every payday field shown in Settings is classified as derived, written, or not settable, from evidence rather than assumption
A value the owner sets in Meridian is verified by READBACK from Crew, and the surface shows the verified value rather than the requested one
A value set in Crew appears in Meridian without a Meridian-side edit, and the freshness of that read is stated
A field that cannot accept a write says so plainly instead of presenting a control that silently does nothing
No write is auto-retried, and an uncertain write is reported as unknown until readback confirms it
The setting is reachable from Settings and nowhere else needs to hold it
tasks.limits: NO NEW FINANCIAL AUTHORITY. This writes a PREFERENCE the owner already owns (his payday rhythm and funding choices), not a movement of money; it must not become a path to transfers or to any proposal-approval bypass. Any write goes through the existing action pipeline if it mutates financial state, and the owner's approval boundaries are unchanged. Crew remains the system of record: Meridian writes what Crew accepts and never keeps a conflicting second copy.
tasks.handoff: meridian/api.py (the two existing /settings/payday routes, 1196 and 1216); templates/meridian/partials/payday-funding.html and static/js/meridian/payday.js (the surface); meridian/services/payday*.py for the read model; templates/meridian/partials/connections.html:16 (the in-page link that is currently the only entry); the Crew adapter used for account reads; OS-048 (bill funding linked to the owner's Funding Cadence) and OS-056 (the deterministic funding schedule), both of which already read payday-derived state and would be affected by any change in where it comes from.
tasks.notes: THE BIDIRECTIONAL HALF IS THE PART THAT WILL BE ASSUMED AWAY IF IT IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN. A one-way write (Meridian -> Crew) plus a cached read would look correct on the surface the owner tests and would silently disagree with Crew the moment he changes it there. The readback discipline in meridian/services/reserves.py -- where the server computes the figure and the client is forbidden from re-deriving it -- is the precedent to follow.
